subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@finlytics.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification

Hi Olivia / Tom —

Great to meet today — thanks for walking through your usage and priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap:
- Current model(s): in-house fork of an open 70B instruction model (similar perf to llama-2-70b), 8k context, some custom system prompts.
- Current monthly consumption: ~600M tokens/month (inference only).
- Growth profile: expect to ramp to ~1.5B tokens/month over 9–12 months based on product roadmap.
- Target latency/SLAs: p95 < 300ms for typical 512-token responses; spike tolerance to 2k tokens/s for short bursts.
- Quality constraints: minimal quantization degradation; happy to explore FP16 or 4-bit but need an eval pass.

Primary qualification questions for pricing/proposal:
1) Target $/1M tokens range you’d be comfortable with as a ballpark? (you mentioned wanting something competitive vs cloud-hosted endpoints)
2) Do you have a GPU preference (H100 vs A100) or constraints from your side?
3) Required sustained throughput (tokens/sec) vs. short peak bursts?

Next steps:
- Dylan will scope recommended HW + sizing options and ballpark pricing for a reserved pool (dedicated).
- I’ll send a short estimate workbook and a follow-up with clarifying questions (attachments).
- If useful, we can set up a technical deep-dive with Marcus (runtime perf) next week.

Please reply with your target $/1M tokens range and any constraints on GPU type or compliance items.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@finlytics.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Target $/1M tokens: We'd like to see something in the range of $40 - $75 / 1M tokens to be viable for our long-term model ops.
- Current confirmed: ~600M tokens/mo today (inference). Expecting 1.5B/mo in ~12 months if adoption goes as forecasted.
- Budget range: roughly $25k - $45k / month at initial scale; would expand as volume increases.
- Preferred GPUs: we don't have a hard requirement but prefer H100-class performance today due to model size and desired latency. A100 could be ok if savings are material and you can demonstrate parity for our workloads.
- Throughput: Target sustained ~800 tokens/sec with ability to handle peaks of ~2000 tokens/sec for short periods.
- Quantization: we can accept 4-bit if you can run our evals and confirm no >3% quality regression on our key prompts.

Would appreciate two ballpark options: a lower-cost pool optimized for cost (more aggressive quantization / batching) and a higher-performance pool (H100s, lower latency). Also send any assumptions you used for $/1M calculations.

Thanks —
Olivia Chen
Head of Product, Finlytics
olivia@finlytics.ai

Hi Olivia / Tom —

Thanks for the clarity — a couple follow-ups from the runtime side so we can size and price accurately: 

1) Model artifacts: can you confirm whether the model is loaded as one shard per GPU or you currently serve sharded across multiple GPUs per request? That impacts our memory/sizing guidance (H100 vs A100).
2) Average response size: you mentioned 512-token responses as common — can you confirm median response length and typical prompt sizes (tokens in prompt + response)?
3) Concurrency pattern: are you running many concurrent short requests (e.g., 50–200 qps at small tokens) or fewer long-running streams?
4) Fallbacks / rollback: do you want an always-on minimally sized pool + autoscale burst credit, or a fixed reserved pool with predictable throughput?

Ballpark capacity assumptions we'll use to produce two pricing options: 
- Option A (performance): 4x H100 reserved pool + small burst slack. Expected sustained throughput ~1,200 tokens/sec (aggregate), p95 latency ~200–300ms for 512-token responses. Price estimate will include dedicated instance cost + support/ops.
- Option B (cost-optimized): 8x A100 reserved pool with more batching and quantization (4-bit) — higher aggregate throughput (~2,400 tokens/sec) but slightly higher p95 due to batching; better $/1M tokens at higher sustained volumes.

We'll run your evals to confirm quality with 4-bit quantization; if regression is >3%, we won't recommend that path. Marcus, can you provide perf numbers for similar workloads so we can include concrete tokens/sec per GPU?

Thanks —
Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia / Tom —

Attached is a short workbook with two ballpark configurations and the unit economics using your current 600M tokens/mo as the baseline. High-level summary below — these are preliminary, non-binding numbers.

Option 1 — Performance (recommended for initial parity)
- HW: 4x H100 (reserved pool)
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~1,200 tokens/sec aggregate; peak burst to ~2,000 tokens/sec with KV caching and burst credits
- Latency: p95 ~200–300ms for 512-token responses
- Monthly price (reserved): $38,000 / month (includes standard support + 99.9% uptime SLA)
- At 600M tokens/mo -> implied ~$63.33 / 1M tokens
- Notes: minimal quantization by default (FP16), will run your evals to confirm quality.

Option 2 — Cost-optimized (higher throughput, batching)
- HW: 8x A100 (reserved pool) with aggressive batching & optional 4-bit quantization
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~2,400 tokens/sec aggregate; p95 latency ~300–400ms depending on batching patterns
- Monthly price (reserved): $68,000 / month (includes support; lower SLA options available to reduce price)
- At 600M tokens/mo -> implied ~$113.33 / 1M tokens (economics improve as tokens grow; at 1.5B/mo this drops to ~$45.33 / 1M)
- Notes: we will validate 4-bit quantization on your eval set — if regression >3% we recommend Option 1 or mixed strategy (H100 pool + burst A100 autoscale).

Assumptions used for calculations (detailed in attached workbook):
- Baseline token conversion based on measured GPU throughput and expected utilization 60–80% for reserved pools.
- Network and operator support included in monthly reserved price.
- Storage and logging retention assumed at standard levels (can be adjusted — will affect price).

Next steps:
1) Olivia / Tom — confirm if you want the eval artifacts (we'll need a sample prompt set + reference outputs) and whether we should proceed with a perf run (we can book a slot next week).
2) If you want to evaluate Option 2's quantization path, share a representative eval set (10–20k prompts) and we'll run quality/latency/perf and return results in 3–4 business days.
3) We can convert either option into a draft order form once you pick a path; Marcus will include explicit tokens/sec per GPU and expected utilization curves in that doc.

If helpful, we'll also schedule a 30-minute tech deep-dive to walk through runtime tradeoffs and autoscaling/burst patterns.

Thanks again — look forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
